name: Kerhanagh

attributes.attribute: an Irish monster whose name means fire-spitter
driven by Patrick from Croagh Patrick
maybe the same as Corra and Caoranach

sources: MacNeill, Máire. "The Festival of Lughnasa, Parts I and II." Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982, 515.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Kerhanagh is an Irish monster. The name is also written Kiraqhna. It means one who spits fire. Folk in the western province of Connacht say Saint Patrick expelled this beast from the great holy hill of Croagh Patrick. The demon then moved across the land and befouled holy wells with its breath. Patrick chased him and almost lost the scent in County Sligo. At a rock beside Tullaghan hill the saint hammered his staff, and fresh water gushed from the stone. Refreshed by the flow, Patrick turned on the monster and won the fight. Some read these tales as the triumph of Christian over pagan ways. Others say Patrick took the place of an earlier hero who drove off bad spirits. Kerhanagh may be the same being as Corra and Caoranach, though the stories are not the same. In English she is sometimes called the Devil's Mother.
